video.title: Generative AI vs AI Agents vs Agentic AI Explained Simply with Example in 5 Mins!

transcript.text: Hi everyone, in this video you will
understand the clear difference between
Gen AI, AI agents and agentic AI with a
real world example. Understanding the
difference between these three is super
important for anyone learning or using
AI tools. So make sure you like this
video and watch it till the end. Let's
imagine you work in a company as a
DevOps engineer and you are given a task
to migrate a microservices application
from virtual machine to Kubernetes by
creating health charts, deploying
services, implementing, monitoring and
also resolving if any issues arise. Now
this task is a complex task that
requires thinking, planning, writing
code, running commands, debugging and
also validating if the migration is
successful or not. Using this example,
let's understand how Gen AI or AI agents
or agentic AI would handle this task and
through this the difference will become
very clear. Let's start with Gen AI. So
Gen AI or generative AI is a type of
artificial intelligence that is trained
on huge massive data sets to generate
new content like text, images, music,
videos, etc. Responding to simple human
prompts. For example, these are all the
popular geni tools used in the market.
Everyone knows about chat GPT and
Claude. If you are a software engineer,
you also know about GitHub copilot. If
you're a designer, you might use Dolly
or Canva AI as well. Popular Gen AI
models like GPT4 or Claude is used by
software engineers to create code,
documentation, even explanations. But
the problem is Gen AI can create
content. It cannot perform actual task
or it cannot interact with the systems.
What do I mean is for example if I give
the same migration task to chat GPT
asking it to help me out it will
generate helm charts yl configuration it
will also create kubernetes manifest
files for deployment it will explain me
all the best practices for migration but
it cannot build the image it cannot
connect to the cluster it cannot run the
commands for me or it cannot verify if
everything is done or not so this is the
flow when working with genai you will
ask what you want and it will generate
the content for you but you have to
implement it you have to run the command
you will also have to fix if there are
any issues. So these Gen AI tools are
smart but they don't plan, they cannot
use APIs, they cannot execute workflows
on their own. You have to do it as a
user. Now let's talk about AI agents. AI
agents are built on top of Gen AI. But
they also have ability to use tools,
call APIs, execute commands and also
interact with system. Which means unlike
Gen AI which can only create content, AI
agents can create content and also take
actions on your behalf. So if I give the
same migration example to an AI agent
created maybe using N10. So it will
generate all the code and the manifest
file required for migration through GNI
capabilities and then also connect to
your cluster using the cubernetes API
and your credentials. Next, it will run
the commands to apply all the changes,
verify if everything is working properly
and also notify you using Slack API.
This means AI agents are able to
understand the prompt given by the user
also decide what steps to take and
actually take actions on your behalf.
But the problem with AI agents are they
are mostly used for single task that
once the task is done AI agents will
stop and that's why using AI agents for
long or complex task is not the right
choice. So you should use agentic AI.
Agentic AI is more advanced and takes
the AI agent concept further by being
fully autonomous which means agentic AI
can work without user instructions for
hours or even for days until the task is
achieved. It also uses multi-step
planning by understanding the complete
goal and breaking them into small
pieces. It has long-term memory also
selfcorrection which means if there are
any issues agentic AI will solve it. Now
unlike AI agent rather than following
stepby-step instruction agentic AI
operates like a self-managed DevOps team
understanding the complete goal doing
things on their own. So they understand
the highle goal and autonomously work
towards them. For example, if I give the
same migration task to an agentic AI,
this is how it will behave. It will
first understand the high level goal
which is to deploy a microser from VM to
Kubernetes. Then create a plan with 10
or 50 subtask. Spin up specialized agent
for specific task and then use different
tools like GitHub, Docker, Cubectl,
Terapform etc. If there are any issues,
it will also fix it on their own. Let's
say if the deployment is failed, it will
also roll back to the previous version.
It will monitor the rollout for
stability. It will also update the
documentation to to include all the
operation that it has done. Create a PR
in GitHub and also notify you on Slack
when everything is done. So, agent AI
does not just complete task, it runs
operation. It will update documentation
for you. It will create pull requests.
It will notify on its own and that's why
it is called as fully autonomous. So, in
short, use Gen AI tools to create
content or code files. Use AI agents for
single specific task and use agentic AI
for long complex operations. I hope this
video was informative. If you have any
questions, any doubt, let me know in the
comment section and subscribe to Cloud
Champ.
